current_example.problem:
| $x$ | $-3$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_{185}$ be a random sample of size $n = 185$ from a population with the probability mass function given above. Find an approximation in terms of $\Phi(z)$ for $P(|\overline{X}| \gt 0.1).$

*Note: $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
current_example.worked_solution:
Suppose that $X_1, X_2,\ldots, X_n$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu$ and population standard deviation $\sigma.$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overline{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overline{X}\sim N\!\left(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n = 185,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =-3\cdot 0.4+(-1)\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.1+3\cdot 0.4 \\  & =-1.2-0.1+0.1+1.2 \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =((-3)^{2}\cdot 0.4+(-1)^{2}\cdot 0.1+{1}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.4)-{0}^{2} \\  & =(3.6+0.1+0.1+3.6)-0 \\  & =7.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0,\frac{7.4}{185}) \\  & ∼N(0,0.04).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(|\overline{X}| \gt 0.1).$ So, we convert $\overline{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.1) & =P(\overset{―}{X}<-0.1)+P(\overset{―}{X}>0.1) \\  & ≈P(Z<\frac{-0.1-0}{\sqrt{0.04}})+P(Z>\frac{0.1-0}{\sqrt{0.04}}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.5)+P(Z>0.5) \\  & =P(Z<-0.5)+1-P(Z<0.5) \\  & =1+Φ(-0.5)-Φ(0.5).\end{aligned}
$$

By the symmetry of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\qquad \Phi(-0.5) 
= 1-\Phi(0.5).
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.1) & =1+Φ(-0.5)-Φ(0.5) \\  & =1+(1-Φ(0.5))-Φ(0.5) \\  & =2-2Φ(0.5) \\  & =2(1-Φ(0.5)).\end{aligned}
$$
